scenarios.name: lazy-validation-failure-report
scenarios.rationale: Both use lazy=True, catch SchemaErrors, and print index/column/check/failure_case; A uses a DataFrameModel-style OrderSchema, but imports it from an external file and never defines it, while B defines a self-contained DataFrameSchema (not a DataFrameModel) and adds csv_line.

scenarios.name: polars-users-data-contract
scenarios.rationale: Response B uses pandera.polars with a DataFrameModel, Field(unique=True, gt=0) and isin, validates pl.read_parquet with lazy=True, and avoids pandas types, so it meets the rubric. Response A hand-rolls the checks in plain Polars and mentions pandera only in passing, so it misses the core requirements.

scenarios.name: orders-schema-cross-column-checks
scenarios.rationale: Response A matches the rubric closely: it uses a pa.DataFrameModel with Field constraints, two @pa.dataframe_check methods that handle null shipped_at, and an inner Config with strict and coerce set to True. Response B uses the DataFrameSchema object API with Check objects and lambda checks. It gets the validation logic right but not the required class-based model, the Field constraints, or the inner Config class, so it only partly meets the rubric.
